content.text: Queen's Slipper 500 is the definitive Australian version of the card game 500, played using specialized decks produced by the iconic Queen's Slipper brand. While standard 500 exists, the Australian variant is unique for its use of 11s, 12s, and 13s, allowing for 4, 5, or even 6-player games with expanded decks. It is a trick-taking game that evolved from Euchre, featuring a complex bidding system, the 'MisÃ¨re' (no-trick) contract, and the inclusion of a Joker as the ultimate trump card.
Originally created in the US in 1904 by the US Playing Card Co. It spread to Australia where the 'Queen's Slipper' brand popularized a variant with expanded suit counts and the MisÃ¨re bid.
43 cards for a 4-handed game: 4s to Aces, plus the Joker and the 11s/12s of specific suits (depends on house rules).

items.text: Joker in No Trumps: Some play that in No Trumps the joker cannot be nominated in advance as belonging to a suit; or that the joker cannot be played on a lead of a suit on which you have previously reneged.
Bidding process: Some allow bidding after pass (auction continues until three passes in succession). Some allow the contractor to raise the final bid after everyone has passed.

Misere ranking and scoring: House rules vary: Misere allowed only after a seven bid; Open Misere ranking between 9 No Trumps and 10 Spades or as highest; alternative scores (e.g. Misere 150, Open Misere 250, misere without pickup 350).
